chunks.text: Pagina 11 van 33 Cells used for cultured meat production are typically adherent cells, meaning that in the in vivo situation they require attachment to a surface. This surface is provided by the extracellular matrix (ECM), an environment outside the cell composed of fibrous proteins and long sugar chains that provide structure and strength to tissues. In bioreactors, however, cultured cells need to grow in suspension. To achieve this, bioreactors often employ so-called microcarriers. These are small beads (approximately 100–400 µm in diameter) to which cells can attach, as the beads mimic the stiffness, porosity, and surface characteristics of the ECM. It is also possible to grow cells on a more complex scaffold. A scaffold is a three-dimensional structure that supports growth, maturation, and differentiation of the culture, facilitating the formation of more complex structures such as multilayered arrangements of cells.
